title: Se pasivo: sistemas de trabajo colonial

sections.content: The se-passive fits labor systems perfectly: a practice that was granted, demanded, or replaced by policy over time, not a single person's one-time decision. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En la encomienda se concedía a un colono español el derecho a la mano de obra de una comunidad indígena.
items.english: Under the encomienda, a Spanish colonist was granted the right to a community's labor.

items.spanish: En 1542 se promulgaron las Leyes Nuevas, que intentaron limitar el poder de los encomenderos.
items.english: In 1542, the New Laws were enacted, which tried to limit the power of the encomenderos.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, se fue sustituyendo la encomienda por el repartimiento.
items.english: Over time, the encomienda was gradually replaced by the repartimiento.

items.spanish: En 1550, en Valladolid, se organizó un debate formal sobre si los indígenas tenían plena condición humana.
items.english: In 1550, in Valladolid, a formal debate was organized over whether indigenous people had full human status.

sections.content: Se fue sustituyendo (with ir + gerund inside the se-construction) marks a gradual replacement, not a sudden one — useful whenever a historical text needs to say 'this slowly gave way to that' rather than 'this stopped and that started'.
